pages.text: Every cat has a place. $(br2)$(li)The $(l)leader$() guides the Clan and takes a name ending in -star.$(li)The $(l)deputy$() sends out patrols.$(li)The $(l)medicine cat$() heals.$(li)$(l)Warriors$() hunt and guard.$(li)$(l)Apprentices$() learn.$(li)$(l)Queens$() raise the kits, and $(l)elders$() share old stories.
pages.title: Clan Ranks

pages.text: In camp you will find nests of soft moss, the fresh-kill pile and the medicine cat's den. $(br2)Bring your catches to the fresh-kill pile so the whole Clan can eat. A full pile in leaf-bare is a gift greater than any victory.
Your Whiskers tell you about any cat near you: their name, their Clan, their rank and how they feel. Use them often. A good warrior knows their Clanmates.

pages.title: Giving Orders
pages.text: A deputy or a leader speaks for the Clan. Talk to a warrior and say $(l)I have orders for you$(): $(br2)$(li)send a patrol round the territory, or out to hunt;$(li)show one cat where to patrol on the map;$(li)or bring a patrol and lead it yourself. $(br2)A patrol you lead fights what you fight. Talk to any of its cats to have them all wait, follow, or go home.

pages.title: Cats of No Clan
pages.text: Not every cat is a Clan cat. Kittypets, loners and rogues will talk if you greet them with an empty paw. A kittypet knows the Twolegplace; a loner hears news from every border. $(br2)A rogue has only threats. Do not turn your back on one. $(br2)If you have no Clan yourself, a loner may ask a favour of you. Keep your word, and even the Clans will hear of it.

pages.title: Your Duties
pages.text: You can hold three duties at once. If your paws are full, any Clanmate you ask for work will let you $(l)set aside$() one of your old duties.
